determinism.identity: the ProblemIR identity is lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical serialized bytes and excludes clocks, process IDs, checkout paths, backend versions, and machine identity
determinism.normalization_boundary: ProblemIR preserves declared operand and reading order; alpha-renaming and commutative semantic normalization are separate MH-044 behavior
determinism.registry_order: entity registries sort by globally unique stable IDs; set-valued references sort and deduplicate, while binder, function-argument, expression-argument, tuple-element, and goal order remains semantic
determinism.serialization: UTF-8 canonical JSON uses NFC strings, sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, no floats, and exactly one trailing newline
determinism.source_spans: half-open zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets are interpreted only against the declared source content SHA-256 and byte length

effects.filesystem: none during construction or serialization; source content and repository paths are never opened through ProblemIR references
effects.mutation: constructed entities and registry tuples are immutable values and caller mappings or sequences are never retained by mutable alias
effects.solver: none; ProblemIR records syntax, typing, readings, and source provenance but carries no mathematical authority

ensures: ProblemIR contains closed registries for source documents, UTF-8 byte spans, domains, variables, expressions, atomic relations, logical or quantified statements, definitions, assumptions, ordered goals, complete readings, one ambiguity state, and namespaced extensions.

Builtin, finite, interval, modular, collection, product, function, and theory-structure domains retain exact element, bound, modulus, factor, parameter, result, totality, and finiteness information without solver-specific objects.

Literal, variable, application, tuple, collection, and conditional expressions carry explicit result domains; equality, order, membership, divisibility, congruence, and named predicates enforce declared arity and compatible operand domains.

Truth, relation, logical, and forall, exists, or exists_unique statement variants form an acyclic graph and preserve binder order, operator argument order, and source order until a separately contracted semantic normalization step.

Source documents expose only media type, language, UTF-8 byte length, and content SHA-256; half-open source spans are bounded by that identity and never depend on a checkout path or platform line ending.
An unambiguous IR selects its sole reading; an unresolved IR never selects silently; a resolved IR selects one declared candidate while retaining every alternative and its structured differences.

Canonical serialization normalizes strings to NFC before construction, rejects floats and non-finite numbers, uses UTF-8 JSON with sorted mapping keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, and one trailing newline, and defines identity as SHA-256 of those exact bytes.
Construction never interprets extensions as core proof semantics, calls a solver, imports legacy reasoning modules, accesses the network, or promotes any mathematical truth claim.

epistemics.ambiguous: two or more complete readings remain visible, none is selected, and the required user choice is explicit
epistemics.invalid: one or more invariants fail and no ProblemIR value or identity is returned
epistemics.mathematical_truth: not claimed; validity of ProblemIR is only validity of representation
epistemics.resolved: one candidate is selected but all alternatives and structured differences remain replayable
epistemics.unambiguous: exactly one complete reading exists and is selected
epistemics.valid: all structural, typing, reference, scope, ambiguity, canonicalization, and budget invariants pass

invariants: The normative schema is docs/contracts/schemas/problem-ir-v1.schema.json=dcf871f15ebbae06b0eca285a115f2545defc00cb0befc23e3cc574d8523df2c and unknown fields fail closed at every object boundary.

Source, span, domain, variable, expression, relation, statement, definition, assumption, goal, and reading IDs share one collision-free namespace, and difference affected_ids are therefore unambiguous.

Finite-domain elements match their declared element domain and cardinality; interval bounds match the builtin base; literal modular moduli exceed one; collection, product, function, and structure references are typed and acyclic.

Variable expressions exactly match variable domains; tuple and collection elements match container domains; conditional branches match the result domain; expression definitions match their non-null result domain and statement definitions declare no result domain.

Integer and rational literal strings have one spelling, rationals are reduced with positive denominator greater than one, booleans are true or false, and approximate floating-point values are not representable in core fields.

Equality uses one exact operand domain, ordered comparisons use ordered numeric domains, divisibility and congruence use integral domains, membership matches the container element domain, and logical or relation arities are exact.
Expression, relation, statement, and domain dependencies contain no cycle; bound and parameter variables cannot escape their owner even through conditional expressions or nested logical statements.
Each ambiguous IR has exactly one base reading and at least one alternative whose difference_from, difference kind, human summary, affected IDs, and source spans remain explicit.
Goal order is preserved independently inside each reading, so multiple goals cannot be reordered by canonical registry sorting.
Extensions may preserve theory-specific annotations but cannot override a core field, introduce an unnamespaced key, contain a float, or change representation validity or mathematical trust.
raises: ProblemIRValidationError with kind schema for unknown or missing fields, malformed tagged unions, invalid enum values, duplicate JSON keys, invalid scalar types, or noncanonical extension values.

ProblemIRValidationError with kind identity, reference, span, domain, expression, literal, relation, statement, definition, cycle, scope, ambiguity, canonical, or budget for the corresponding failed invariant.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit are never converted into an ordinary invalid-ProblemIR result.
requires: Input is a schema-exact mathhead.problem-ir.v1 object governed by docs/contracts/schemas/problem-ir-v1.schema.json=dcf871f15ebbae06b0eca285a115f2545defc00cb0befc23e3cc574d8523df2c.
Every registry is sorted by stable ASCII ID, every ID is globally unique, every reference resolves to the declared registry kind, and the combined entity count does not exceed 100000.

All strings are Unicode NFC without NUL, all mathematical numeric literals use canonical exact strings, JSON numeric values are bounded integers only, and extensions use explicit reverse-DNS namespaces.
Bound variables have exactly one quantified-statement owner, definition parameters have exactly one definition owner, and neither kind appears outside its lexical statement or definition scope.
Every reading names a complete ordered goal list and its definition and assumption sets; unresolved ambiguity contains at least two readings, no selected reading, and an explicit required choice.
signature: ProblemIR(*, schema: str, source_documents: tuple[SourceDocument, ...], source_spans: tuple[SourceSpan, ...], domains: tuple[Domain, ...], variables: tuple[Variable, ...], expressions: tuple[Expression, ...], relations: tuple[Relation, ...], statements: tuple[Statement, ...], definitions: tuple[Definition, ...], assumptions: tuple[Assumption, ...], goals: tuple[Goal, ...], readings: tuple[Reading, ...], ambiguity: Ambiguity, extensions: Mapping[str, CanonicalValue]) -> None
